<!-- Generated by Ankus.DocGenerator. -->

Namespace: [Ankus](/api/ankus/)

Assembly: `Ankus.Runtime.dll`

Represents PostgreSQL date, including BC dates, its full finite range, and both infinities.
The default value is 2000-01-01.

```csharp
[JsonConverter(typeof(PgDateConverter))]
public readonly struct PgDate : IComparable<PgDate>, IParsable<PgDate>, IEquatable<PgDate>
```

Implements: [IComparable&lt;PgDate&gt;](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.icomparable-1), [IParsable&lt;PgDate&gt;](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.iparsable-1), [IEquatable&lt;PgDate&gt;](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.iequatable-1)

### TryParse(string?, out PgDate)

Tries to parse PostgreSQL date syntax on the active backend thread.

```csharp
public static bool TryParse(string? text, out PgDate value)
```

Parameters:

`text` — [string](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.string)

The date text.

`value` — [PgDate](/api/ankus.pgdate/)

The parsed date, or the default value on invalid input.

Returns: [bool](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.boolean)

Whether the input is valid. Backend-access and operational errors still throw.

Invalid input leaves no error pending: PostgreSQL 16 and later report it as a soft input error, and earlier majors
roll back an internal subtransaction. Before PostgreSQL 16, transaction callbacks and parallel operations forbid
that rollback; native errors there remain pending and throw PgException.
